headline: Revenue -5.5% but adjusted EPS $0.42 doubles estimates on full-price selling; Capri lifts FY27 to ~$3.42B / ~$2.20 EPS.
guidance_note: FY27 revenue ~ $3.42B (from ~$3.40B), adj. EPS ~ $2.20 (from ~$2.15); Q3 revenue ~ $1.005B vs ~$1.02B consensus; MK to grow again in Q4.
key_messages: Michael Kors revenue -8.6% (-8.0% cc) to $663M: Americas -11%, EMEA -5%, Asia -1%; inventory delays cost ~ $50M.
MK gross margin 61.5% (+220 bps) on higher full-price sell-throughs and lower tariff rates; markdowns and promotions cut deliberately.
Jimmy Choo +11.5% (+12.2% cc) to $146M, Americas up >20%; MK customer database +8%.
~$20M of wholesale shipments pulled forward from Q3 into Q2.
Idol cited the earlier price reset and possible small MK full-price increases.

consumer.big_ticket: MK demand still shrinking in the Americas as Capri pulls back from discount channels; Jimmy Choo (higher-end) growing.
consumer.pricing: Fewer promotions and markdowns; lower tariff rates helped margins; possible minor MK price increases.
consumer.quote: "We are encouraged by the consumer response to our new product introductions and the progress we are seeing across both Michael Kors and Jimmy Choo." (management, Q2 call)

macro_read: Lower-priced aspirational luxury (Michael Kors) is still losing US sales as it cuts discounting, while the pricier Jimmy Choo grows, consistent with stronger spending at the higher end.
notes: Growth is as reported; Capri gives no constant-currency figure for the Americas. Versace was sold to Prada in December 2025; Jimmy Choo is still part of Capri.
Continuing operations = Michael Kors + Jimmy Choo. Only Versace was sold to Prada (closed Dec 2025); Jimmy Choo remains in Capri's continuing operations.
Stock surged on report day but sources disagree (Reuters >19% intraday; ~15.5-16% elsewhere); close not confirmed, so null.
Revenue consensus null: sources disagree ($781.7M Zacks to $786.6M MarketBeat).
GAAP EPS $0.25 vs adjusted $0.42. Gross margin bps is company-wide (63.3% vs 61.0%).
The headline figure is Michael Kors Americas revenue, -11% as reported by management.
